answer: Latency-Seeded Admission Windows. Each identity must solve a unique, delayed proof-of-work challenge whose difficulty is seeded by live network state (like tundra sensor feeds) and released only in narrow time windows. Cloning forces attackers to pay real compute plus idle wait time per identity, and missed windows forfeit a karst-verified deposit. Because marginal clones add latency without yield, each extra identity is strictly negative-EV, throttling nebula-scale farms.
